page.topic: Smart hospital room management (EcoStruxure Connected Room Solutions for Healthcare)
target_prompts: What is a smart hospital room management solution and what does it do?
fan_out: Which room functions does it control (HVAC, lighting, blinds, nurse call, wayfinding)?
Which components make up the solution (controllers, sensors, BMS software)?
How does it integrate with nurse-call, clinical and third-party building systems?
What measurable outcomes (energy, length of stay, staff time) does it deliver, with evidence?
Which standards apply (e.g. ASHRAE 170 for ventilation / infection control)?

criteria.rationale: No quantified outcomes; benefit headings only.
Room-level applications with context and third-party integration; no scope boundaries or fit guidance.
Components named with roles (SpaceLogic RP-C, SE8000, sensors, EcoStruxure Building Operation) but integration only as bullets, no protocols, no technical parameter (c1+c4 fail -> <= 2).
No phases, delivery roles or timeline.
Mostly functional description but framed as 'why choose our'; no limitations; light hype only.
Lead sentence names the solution and what it does; H1 matches the prompt; H2s open with slogans, no summary block.
Descriptive benefit headings and persona lists, short paragraphs; product cards are '...'-truncated and cloned, persona headings rendered as H1s, component details in hidden tabs.
Undated; problem statistics from 2019-2022 with no review date.
Defines the solution and covers functions, components, integration and ASHRAE 170; lacks outcome evidence, references and how-to-start facts.
What, who and when are clear in the top block; outcome is unquantified ('increases energy efficiency').
Problem statistics sourced with organisation and year; ASHRAE 170 cited; no quotes, first-party evidence or owner.
Segment problems stated in the top block with three quantified, footnoted, sourced statistics (WHO, HCWH/ARUP 2019, TechTarget 2022).
Consideration-level solution explanation per persona with descriptive product CTAs.

warnings: U3: judge proposed 3 but checks support max 2; using 2
U3: level 3 -> 2 (rubric cap: key facts only in image/video/PDF/tab/widget (framework U3 rule, R2)); using 2
U5: level 2 -> 3 (anchor: checks meet the level-3 definition (judge proposed 2)); using 3
